domain_label: Personal Media Manager (Instagram) — Positioning From Zero & Format Strategy
purpose: The method an expert Instagram media manager reasons through when starting the owner's two-persona classic-luxurious motivation+luxury account from zero: locking the niche and translating a 'what do I want to become' brief into a content-identity system (name field, bio, grid, highlights), deciding one-account-vs-two for the two AI personas, and assigning Reels/carousels/Stories their roles strictly against what Instagram has officially said (Mosseri statements, the ranking-explainer page, Meta creator-blog mechanics) while keeping a hard folklore firewall against unsourced creator-guru claims and never inventing an engagement statistic, platform policy or study result the grounding research did not carry.
assumptions: no live Insights dataset or benchmark is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior, and every platform claim is quoted from the grounding research file's fetched or excerpted sources, not re-derived here

every official Meta/Instagram domain (about.instagram.com, about.fb.com, help.instagram.com, transparency.meta.com) returned HTTP 403 to the research agent this session and web.archive.org was also blocked; official claims are carried as [FACT-excerpt] — grounded in search-result excerpts of the named official page plus ≥2 independent secondary sources — and must be re-verified against the cited official URL before any compliance-critical action, never silently upgraded to plain FACT

third-party format/engagement benchmarks (Socialinsider, Buffer, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Later aggregate studies) are ESTIMATE-tier: cross-industry averages biased toward US/EU business audiences, carried with their stated confidence, never equated with an Instagram ranking rule

the folklore firewall is load-bearing throughout this KB: any creator-guru claim with no located official statement (e.g. fixed 'engagement window' rules, per-day Reels posting caps) is tagged UNKNOWN/folklore and never encoded as a hard rule, per the research file's explicit anti-folklore note

Higgsfield model names, ids, parameters, durations, aspect ratios and media roles are out of this KB's scope entirely — they belong to the movie-studio production specialists and are never asserted here from memory
exclusions: quote sourcing, attribution ethics, copyright/public-domain rules for motivational lines (owned by the content/quote-craft specialist; this KB only fixes WHERE a quote lives in the identity system, not how it is cleared)

the news-to-content conversion loop's scenario/brief-generation mechanics and the weekly analytics review's ranking-and-routing math beyond the format-assignment signals this KB is built on (owned by the analytics/operations specialist)
the character-consistency specialist's persona-bible internals (wardrobe/hair/grade construction) — this KB only fixes that the media manager CONSUMES that bible and never improvises it

compliance topics beyond the AI-info self-label, impersonation boundary and recommendation-eligibility line that this KB's positioning/format decisions directly touch (branded-content/paid-partnership rules, FTC disclosure, and the celebrity/right-of-publicity boundary live in dedicated compliance and psychologist-specialist files)

the detailed week-by-week content calendar and per-slot scenario bindings (an operations/calendar artifact that consumes this KB's format-division-of-labor and cadence-baseline nodes, not a node of this KB itself)
asserting a specific Instagram algorithm penalty ladder, exact engagement-drop percentage, or any other number the grounding file marked UNKNOWN as if it had been fetched

competency_questions.question: What is the account's locked niche and how does the owner's 'what do I want to become' brief translate into a content-identity statement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICHE_DEFINITION_LOCK names the hybrid motivation+luxury(+fitness-accent) pillar, the classic-luxurious register, and the cinematic-production-value differentiator (tagged ESTIMATE where the comparison is a strategic judgment, not a measured result), and ASPIRATIONAL_IDENTITY_TRANSLATION states the identity-statement must be specific enough to constrain bio/grid/highlight choices

competency_questions.question: How are the two AI personas (male + female) structured, and should they run on one account or two?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TWO_PERSONA_ARCHITECTURE names the male+female persona structure per the owner brief, and ACCOUNT_STRUCTURE_DECISION states the default (one flagship account housing both personas) plus the explicit Insights-based trigger condition for splitting later, never a split on anecdote alone

competency_questions.question: What goes in the name field and bio, and why does keyword placement there matter?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NAME_FIELD_KEYWORD_SEO states that Instagram search matches name-field and bio keywords (a [FACT-excerpt] behavior confirmed via reported Mosseri statements) and gives a concrete keyword-in-name-field example, and BIO_SKELETON_DESIGN gives the 3-line bio skeleton (category promise / both personas named / CTA)

competency_questions.question: How is the grid's visual contract locked, and what does the highlight taxonomy look like?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRID_VISUAL_CONTRACT states the first 9-12 posts define the visual contract via a locked classic-luxe color-grade LUT family, and HIGHLIGHT_TAXONOMY enumerates the six proposed highlight categories (Him/Her/Places/Cars/Quotes/BTS-AI)

competency_questions.question: Why must the media manager consume rather than improvise the persona bible, and how does the BTS-AI highlight function as voluntary transparency?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSONA_BIBLE_CONSUMPTION states the bio/grid promises must match the character-consistency specialist's locked wardrobe/hair/grade, and AI_TRANSPARENCY_HIGHLIGHT explains the BTS-AI highlight lowers deception/impersonation risk as voluntary disclosure distinct from the mandatory per-post label

competency_questions.question: In what precise sense is there no single Instagram algorithm, and what does that mean for format strategy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NO_SINGLE_ALGORITHM_MODEL states, per Instagram's official Ranking Explained post [FACT-excerpt], that Feed, Stories, Explore and Reels each run their own ranking system tuned to how people use that surface, so a single 'the algorithm' framing is a category error

competency_questions.question: What are the three signals Mosseri named as most important for reach, and how do they split between follower and non-follower reach?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOSSERI_TOP_SIGNALS names watch time, likes-per-reach and sends(DM shares)-per-reach [FACT-excerpt — Mosseri Jan 2025 statements], and NON_FOLLOWER_VS_FOLLOWER_REACH_SPLIT states sends-per-reach is the strongest non-follower signal while likes-per-reach matters more for connected/follower reach

competency_questions.question: Do hashtags drive reach, and what should captions do instead now that public content is search-indexed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HASHTAGS_DO_NOT_DRIVE_REACH states hashtags categorize but do not meaningfully increase reach per repeated Mosseri statements [FACT-excerpt], and CAPTION_SEARCH_SURFACE states captions/bio/alt-text keywords drive search and, since ~July 2025, public professional-account content is Google/Bing indexable [FACT-excerpt]

competency_questions.question: Why must every exported Reel be watermark-clean, and what production consequence does that carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WATERMARK_RECOMMENDATION_PENALTY states visible third-party watermarks make Reels less likely to be recommended [ESTIMATE — widely reported official guidance, official page unfetched this session] and ties this to requiring clean, watermark-free renders from the production pipeline

competency_questions.question: What role does each format (Reels, carousels, Stories) play in the growth engine, and what do third-party benchmarks add on top of the platform-stated signals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_DIVISION_OF_LABOR states the working rule Reels=discovery, carousels=depth/saves, Stories=retention (with Stories-ranked-by-closeness sourced [FACT-excerpt] and the division itself [ESTIMATE]), and THIRD_PARTY_FORMAT_BENCHMARKS gives the Socialinsider reach-vs-engagement-rate figures as ESTIMATE-tier context, not ranking fact

competency_questions.question: What exactly is the folklore firewall, and which specific claims has this research already flagged as folklore?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOLKLORE_FIREWALL_DISCIPLINE states that claims like fixed 'first-30-minutes engagement window' rules or per-day Reels posting caps have no located official source and are excluded from the standing playbook, and gives the tag-before-encode discipline (FACT/FACT-excerpt/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN) that applies to every downstream rule

competency_questions.question: What is the cadence baseline, and how do the AI-disclosure and impersonation boundaries constrain the two personas' presentation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CADENCE_BASELINE_SUSTAINABLE gives Mosseri's stated baseline (a couple of feed posts/week + 1-2 Stories/day) and his sustainability-over-optimization caveat [FACT-excerpt], AI_INFO_LABEL_COMPLIANCE states photoreal AI video is in Meta's mandatory-disclosure class [FACT-excerpt] so this account always self-labels, and IMPERSONATION_BOUNDARY_FOR_PERSONAS states both personas must present as original AI personas, never as any real individual

glossary.definition: The owner-brief-specified hybrid pillar this account commits to: motivational quotes-with-video plus luxury lifestyle (cars, places, travel) in a classic-luxurious register with occasional fitness accents, run through two AI personas [FACT — OWNER_BRIEF.md §2b.9, §2b.12]. The differentiator against similar creator archetypes is cinematic production value, not a measured performance edge [ESTIMATE].

The structural decision to run one male and one female AI persona as the account's recurring on-screen cast, with account-structure (one account vs. two) treated as a separate, later-revisable decision [ESTIMATE — design options, not platform fact].

The name field, bio, grid (first 9-12 posts) and highlight taxonomy treated as one coherent visual/textual contract with the viewer, distinct from any single post [ESTIMATE — craft convention, high adoption among professional accounts].

Instagram's official framing that Feed, Stories, Explore and Reels each have their own ranking system tuned to that surface's usage pattern, so 'the Instagram algorithm' (singular) is a category error [FACT-excerpt — about.instagram.com Ranking Explained, proxy-blocked this session, excerpts consistently reported by secondary sources].

The ratio of DM shares to reach; per Mosseri's Jan 2025 statements the strongest signal for reaching non-followers, distinct from likes-per-reach which matters more for connected/follower reach [FACT-excerpt].

The binding discipline that any creator-guru or practitioner claim with no located official Instagram/Meta statement (e.g. a fixed 'first 30 minutes' engagement window, a per-day Reels posting cap) is tagged folklore/UNKNOWN and never encoded as a hard rule in the standing playbook, no matter how widely repeated [design discipline, directly required by this KB's grounding research §2.2].

Meta's post-May-2024 labeling regime: an 'AI info' label applied when industry-standard AI indicators are detected or the poster self-discloses, with disclosure REQUIRED for photorealistic generated video or realistic synthetic audio; the exact penalty ladder for non-disclosure is unpublished [FACT-excerpt for the requirement; UNKNOWN for the penalty ladder].

A toggle (launched Dec 10, 2024) that shows a Reel to non-followers only, skipping followers' feeds and the grid, with comparative performance surfaced ~24h later and eligibility gated at ≥1,000 followers [FACT-excerpt]; used here as the A/B lab for hook/format/persona experiments once the account clears that follower gate.

The locked color-grade LUT family (warm neutrals, deep blacks) the grid commits to across its first 9-12 posts so the profile reads as one film; must be cross-checked against the character-consistency specialist's persona bible rather than set independently [ESTIMATE — craft convention].

nodes.definition: Lock the account's niche as a hybrid pillar per the owner brief: motivational quotes-with-video plus luxury lifestyle (cars, places, travel) in a classic-luxurious register, with fitness accents used sometimes, executed through two AI personas, one male and one female [FACT — OWNER_BRIEF.md §2b.9, §2b.12]. The strategic read is that a hybrid motivation-times-luxury-travel account is a recognized creator archetype, and the differentiator against existing accounts in that space is cinematic production value from a movie-studio pipeline rather than stock-footage montages [ESTIMATE — strategic judgment, medium confidence; no fetched study compares hybrid vs single-pillar niche performance]. Locking this niche precisely — not 'lifestyle content' in general — is what lets every downstream identity, format and analytics decision be evaluated against a fixed target rather than drifting wider over time.

included: the hybrid pillar definition (motivation + luxury cars/places/travel, classic-luxurious register, occasional fitness accent)
the two-AI-persona (male+female) structural constraint
the production-value differentiation logic
excluded: the specific scenario bank or shot lists (movie-studio pipeline's remit)
the identity-system execution of the niche (its own nodes)

pros.claim: A hybrid pillar with a stated production-value differentiator gives the account a defensible identity distinct from stock-footage motivation pages
pros.example: positioning against generic quote pages by leading with cinematic movie-studio-grade footage of the luxury/travel beats

cons.claim: The hybrid-vs-pure-niche comparison is an unverified strategic judgment, not a measured result, so the niche choice itself carries real uncertainty
cons.example: assuming the hybrid niche outperforms a pure luxury or pure motivation account without any fetched study to confirm it

failure_modes: drifting the niche wider over time (adding pillars) until the account reads as generic lifestyle content
treating the niche as flexible per-post rather than a fixed contract the identity system must honor
revisit_triggers: Insights show the hybrid niche underperforming a narrower pillar after a full analytics cycle
the owner brief's niche parameters (§2b.9/2b.12) are revised
a fitness-accent post drifts the account's perceived category away from luxury/motivation

base.update_signal: the owner brief's niche parameters change or Insights show the hybrid niche underperforming a narrower pillar

nodes.definition: Translate the owner's 'what do I want to become' aspirational brief into an operational content-identity statement that the bio, grid and highlights can each be checked against. The niche lock names WHAT the account is about; this node names WHO the account is being for the viewer — the felt promise ('cinematic motivation and luxury living, told through two personas') that every subsequent identity-system artifact must honor. This is a design translation step, not a platform fact [ESTIMATE — strategic synthesis of the niche lock and the owner brief, no external source]. Without this explicit statement, the bio, grid and highlights risk being independently 'good' while not adding up to one coherent identity.

included: the translation step from aspirational brief to a checkable identity statement
the requirement that bio/grid/highlights each be checkable against this statement
excluded: the niche's content pillars themselves (NICHE_DEFINITION_LOCK)
the specific bio/grid/highlight artifacts (their own nodes)

pros.claim: An explicit identity statement gives the bio, grid and highlights one shared target instead of three independently 'good' but uncoordinated artifacts
pros.example: checking a proposed grid LUT against the identity statement's felt promise before locking it, rather than judging the LUT purely on its own merits

cons.claim: A vague or overly abstract identity statement fails to actually constrain anything, defeating the point of the translation step
cons.example: writing 'aspirational and premium' as the identity statement, which is too generic to rule any bio or grid choice out

failure_modes: writing an identity statement generic enough that any bio/grid/highlight choice satisfies it
skipping the translation step and letting each identity-system artifact be designed independently
revisit_triggers: the owner's aspirational brief changes
a bio/grid/highlight review finds artifacts that no longer read as one coherent identity
the two-persona architecture changes in a way that shifts what the account is 'for'

base.update_signal: the owner's aspirational brief changes or an identity-coherence review fails

nodes.definition: Fix the two-AI-persona structure the whole positioning system is built around: one male persona and one female persona as the account's recurring on-screen cast, per the owner brief [FACT — OWNER_BRIEF.md §2b.9]. This is a structural given, not a design choice this KB questions; what IS a design choice is everything downstream — whether the two personas share an account (ACCOUNT_STRUCTURE_DECISION), how the highlight taxonomy names them ('Him'/'Her'), and how the bio introduces both. Treating the two-persona structure as fixed prevents downstream nodes from re-litigating it and keeps them focused on execution.

included: the male+female persona structure as a fixed owner-brief given
why downstream nodes treat it as fixed rather than re-litigating it
excluded: the account-structure decision of one vs two accounts (its own node)
the persona bible's wardrobe/hair/grade content (character-consistency specialist)

pros.claim: Treating the two-persona structure as fixed lets every downstream identity/format node focus on execution rather than re-arguing the premise
pros.example: the highlight taxonomy simply naming 'Him'/'Her' categories instead of debating whether two personas are warranted

cons.claim: Locking the structure this early forecloses learning from early data that a single-persona or different-persona-mix account might perform better
cons.example: discovering after months that one persona drives nearly all growth, by which point the identity system is already built around both

failure_modes: silently dropping one persona in execution while still presenting the account as two-persona in the bio/highlights
re-litigating the two-persona premise inside downstream nodes instead of treating it as fixed
revisit_triggers: the owner brief changes the persona count or genders
the account-structure decision resolves to split, changing how the two personas are presented
sustained analytics show one persona structurally outperforming the other

base.update_signal: the owner brief changes persona count/genders or sustained analytics show one persona structurally outperforming the other

nodes.definition: Decide whether the two personas run on one shared account (both as a recurring cast) or on two separate accounts cross-promoted via Collab posts [ESTIMATE — design options, not platform fact]. The honest trade-off: two accounts double the content burden and split early momentum, while one account risks muddying persona-specific audience appeal (a male-attractor vs female-attractor split the psychologist specialist's remit covers). The defensible cold-start default is one flagship account with both personas, splitting later ONLY if Insights show a real follower-segment divergence [ESTIMATE — reasoned recommendation, medium confidence]. Whether Meta's optional 'AI creator' profile label changes reach by account type is unresolved [UNKNOWN — no published reach data by account-label type was found].

included: the one-account vs two-account trade-off and the default-plus-trigger recommendation
the unresolved AI-creator-label-by-account-type question
excluded: the two-persona structure itself (its own node)
the Collab-post mechanics used if the account later splits (edge-level content)

pros.claim: Starting on one flagship account preserves shared early momentum and halves the content burden versus running two accounts from zero
pros.example: one account's first month of posts building a single follower base instead of splitting nascent reach across two grids

cons.claim: A shared account risks diluting persona-specific audience appeal if the male- and female-attractor content pull genuinely different audiences
cons.example: a follower who came for the male persona's car content unfollowing after a run of female-persona posts that don't match their interest

failure_modes: splitting the account early on anecdote or preference rather than a documented Insights-based divergence trigger
never revisiting the decision even after Insights show a clear follower-segment split
revisit_triggers: Insights show a statistically meaningful follower-segment divergence between the two personas (minimum 3 posts per cell, per the weekly-review small-sample discipline)
Meta publishes reach data by AI-creator-label account type
the owner brief revises the persona-count or account-count preference

base.update_signal: Insights show a real follower-segment divergence or Meta publishes AI-creator-label reach data by account type

nodes.definition: Put searchable keywords in the profile's NAME field (distinct from the @handle), e.g. 'Name | Luxury Motivation', because Instagram search matches name-field and bio keywords where hashtags do not [FACT-excerpt — keyword-search behavior confirmed via reported Mosseri statements]. This is the identity system's first discovery lever and is authored jointly with the bio skeleton so the two do not duplicate or contradict each other. The craft convention of WHERE exactly to place keywords in the name field (before/after a pipe, brand-name-first vs keyword-first) is a practitioner convention, not a platform-documented format [ESTIMATE — craft convention].

included: the name-field-vs-handle distinction
the keyword-in-name-field search-matching fact
the pipe-separated example convention
excluded: the bio's line-by-line content (its own node)
hashtag strategy (its own node)

pros.claim: Keyword placement in the name field costs nothing and directly exploits a confirmed Instagram search-matching behavior
pros.example: a search for 'luxury motivation' surfacing the account because the phrase sits in the name field, not because of a hashtag

cons.claim: Over-stuffing the name field with keywords can read as spammy and undercut the classic-luxurious brand tone the identity system is built around
cons.example: a name field crammed with five keyword phrases instead of the one clean category phrase the identity statement calls for

failure_modes: treating the @handle as the keyword surface instead of the name field
stuffing keywords past the point of readability

base.update_signal: Instagram changes how name-field search-matching works or a keyword-stuffing complaint surfaces

nodes.definition: Write the bio as a fixed 3-line skeleton: line 1 the category promise (e.g. 'Cinematic motivation & luxury living'), line 2 naming both personas, line 3 a CTA/link [ESTIMATE — practitioner convention]. This must directly reflect the identity statement from ASPIRATIONAL_IDENTITY_TRANSLATION and must not contradict the two-persona architecture by omitting either persona. The bio and the name-field keyword phrase are authored in the same pass so they read as one identity string rather than two independently drafted pieces of copy.

included: the 3-line skeleton (category promise / both personas / CTA)
the requirement to author bio and name-field keyword phrase together
excluded: the name-field keyword mechanics themselves (its own node)
the highlight taxonomy the bio's promises feed into (its own node)

pros.claim: A fixed 3-line skeleton keeps the bio legible and on-identity instead of drifting into generic lifestyle-account copy
pros.example: checking a bio draft line-by-line against the skeleton and catching a missing persona mention before publish

cons.claim: A rigid 3-line template can feel formulaic next to hand-crafted bios from established creator accounts
cons.example: the bio reading as a template-filled identity card rather than a distinctive voice, if the copy inside each line is generic

failure_modes: naming only one persona in line 2, contradicting the two-persona architecture
drafting the bio and name-field phrase separately so they duplicate or conflict

base.update_signal: the identity statement changes or a bio review finds the two personas unevenly represented

nodes.definition: Lock a single classic-luxe color-grade LUT family (warm neutrals, deep blacks) across the first 9-12 grid posts so the profile reads as one film rather than a scattered set of clips [ESTIMATE — craft convention, aligned with the color-grading specialist's remit]. This grid visual contract is the identity system's most durable artifact: it is what a new visitor's grid preview promises before they read a single caption, so it must be cross-checked against the character-consistency specialist's persona bible (locked wardrobe/hair/grade) rather than set independently, and must visibly deliver the identity statement's felt promise.

included: the locked classic-luxe LUT family across the first 9-12 posts
the requirement to cross-check the grid against the persona bible
the grid as the visitor's first-impression contract
excluded: the persona bible's own construction (character-consistency specialist)
the highlight taxonomy that sits below the grid (its own node)

pros.claim: A locked LUT family across the first grid run makes the profile read as one coherent film to a new visitor within seconds
pros.example: a visitor's grid preview showing 9 posts in one consistent warm-neutral, deep-black grade instead of nine unrelated color treatments

cons.claim: Locking the grade this early can force awkward retrofits later if the persona bible's wardrobe/grade is revised after posts are already live
cons.example: a bible revision landing after the first 9 posts publish, leaving the grid visibly split between two grades

failure_modes: setting the LUT family independently of the persona bible and having it drift from the locked character look
changing the grade mid-run without framing it as a deliberate reset
revisit_triggers: the persona bible's wardrobe/hair/grade is revised after the grid has already published posts under the old grade
a grid-coherence review finds posts that visibly break the locked LUT family
the identity statement changes in a way that implies a different visual register

base.update_signal: a persona-bible revision lands after posts publish or a grid-coherence review finds a broken grade

nodes.definition: Build the highlight taxonomy: 'Him', 'Her', 'Places', 'Cars', 'Quotes', 'Behind the scenes (AI)' [ESTIMATE — design proposal]. The first four categories reflect the two-persona and niche structure directly; the 'Behind the scenes (AI)' highlight is the deliberate AI-transparency surface (its own node covers why). The taxonomy is authored after the bio skeleton exists so the highlight names echo the bio's stated promise rather than inventing a parallel vocabulary.

included: the six proposed highlight categories and their rationale
the requirement that highlight names echo the bio's vocabulary
excluded: the BTS-AI highlight's transparency function specifically (its own node)
the grid's visual contract that sits above the highlights (its own node)

pros.claim: A six-category taxonomy gives a new visitor an immediate map of the account's content without scrolling the grid
pros.example: a visitor tapping 'Cars' or 'Places' directly instead of hunting through the feed for a specific pillar

cons.claim: A fixed six-category taxonomy can feel arbitrary if actual posting volume skews heavily toward one or two categories
cons.example: a 'Cars' highlight with only two saved stories next to a 'Quotes' highlight with fifty, reading as unbalanced

failure_modes: inventing highlight names that don't match the bio's stated vocabulary
leaving a highlight category empty long enough that it reads as abandoned

base.update_signal: posting volume skews heavily enough that a category should be merged or split

nodes.definition: Fix the dependency rule between this KB and the movie-studio pipeline: the media manager CONSUMES the character-consistency specialist's locked wardrobe/hair/grade persona bible and never improvises it independently [FACT — pipeline architecture per OWNER_BRIEF.md §2b.6]. Every bio and grid promise about the two personas' look must be cross-checked against that bible before it is published; if the bio or grid implies a look the bible does not define, the bible is revised upstream, not silently reinterpreted downstream. This is the single highest-leverage cross-topic coupling in the identity system, since a mismatch here corrupts both the grid's visual contract and the account's impersonation/transparency posture.

included: the consume-not-improvise dependency rule
the requirement to cross-check every bio/grid look-claim against the bible
why a mismatch here corrupts downstream identity artifacts
excluded: the persona bible's own content/construction (character-consistency specialist's remit)
the grid's LUT-lock execution (its own node)

pros.claim: Treating the persona bible as the single source of truth for persona look prevents the identity system from silently drifting from the movie-studio pipeline's character consistency
pros.example: catching a bio draft that implies a hairstyle the bible does not define, before it publishes and creates a visible mismatch

cons.claim: A strict consume-only rule slows identity-system iteration when the media manager notices a look opportunity the bible has not yet captured
cons.example: wanting to promote a new wardrobe combo in the bio before the bible has formally locked it, and having to wait for the upstream update

failure_modes: the media manager improvising a persona detail in the bio or grid that the bible never defined
publishing grid content under a persona look the bible has since revised without updating the grid artifact
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the media manager consumes rather than improvises the persona bible, and shows a cross-check step verifying every bio/grid persona-look claim against the bible before publish
revisit_triggers: the persona bible is revised
a bio or grid draft is found to imply a persona-look detail the bible does not define
the character-consistency specialist reports a mismatch between published content and the locked bible

base.update_signal: the persona bible is revised or a bio/grid mismatch against it is found

nodes.definition: Use the 'Behind the scenes (AI)' highlight as voluntary, identity-system-level transparency about the pipeline, distinct from the mandatory per-post AI-info label [ESTIMATE — design proposal, consistent with the mandatory-disclosure fact carried in AI_INFO_LABEL_COMPLIANCE]. Where the per-post label is a compliance requirement enforced post-by-post, the BTS-AI highlight is a standing, visitor-facing surface that frames the AI pipeline as part of the account's craft story rather than something to hide, which both lowers deception/impersonation risk and gives the audience a place to see the production value the niche's differentiator claims.

included: the BTS-AI highlight's voluntary, standing-transparency function
its distinction from the mandatory per-post AI-info label
how it supports the niche's production-value differentiator
excluded: the mandatory per-post label mechanics themselves (its own node)
the highlight taxonomy's other five categories (its own node)

pros.claim: A standing BTS-AI highlight turns a compliance obligation into a craft-story asset that supports the account's cinematic-production-value differentiator
pros.example: a visitor tapping the BTS-AI highlight and seeing the pipeline framed as the account's distinguishing craft, not a disclaimer buried in captions

cons.claim: A highlight can be under-updated relative to per-post labels, creating a gap between what a specific post discloses and what the standing highlight shows
cons.example: the BTS-AI highlight going stale for months while individual posts' labels remain current, understating how central the AI pipeline is

failure_modes: treating the BTS-AI highlight as a substitute for the mandatory per-post label rather than a complement to it
letting the highlight go stale relative to the current pipeline

base.update_signal: the highlight is found stale relative to current pipeline practice or is mistaken for the mandatory label

nodes.definition: Establish the foundational ranking model for all format decisions: Instagram's official 'Instagram Ranking Explained' post states there is no single algorithm — Feed, Stories, Explore and Reels each have their own ranking system tuned to how people use that surface [FACT-excerpt — official page proxy-blocked this session, consistently reported by multiple secondary sources]. Treating 'the algorithm' as one monolithic system is a category error every downstream format decision must avoid; a claim true for Reels ranking is not automatically true for Stories ranking, and vice versa.

included: the official no-single-algorithm framing
that each surface (Feed/Stories/Explore/Reels) has its own ranking system
excluded: the specific signals within each ranking system (their own nodes)
the format-strategy assignments this framing enables (its own node)

pros.claim: Naming the per-surface ranking structure prevents a Reels-specific finding from being mis-applied to Stories or Feed strategy
pros.example: recognizing that a Reels watch-time finding does not automatically govern how Stories (ranked by relationship/closeness) should be used

cons.claim: The per-surface framing is stated at a high level in the official post; the exact per-surface signal weightings are not published in full
cons.example: knowing Stories ranks by relationship/closeness in general terms without a published exact weighting formula

failure_modes: treating a Reels-specific ranking finding as if it applied uniformly across all surfaces
citing 'the Instagram algorithm' as a singular system in strategy documents
revisit_triggers: Instagram publishes a revised or more detailed ranking-explainer post
the proxy block on Meta domains lifts and the official page can be fetched directly for re-verification

edge_cases.description: A creator-guru claim with no located official statement is proposed for the standing calendar.
edge_cases.trigger: a practitioner source asserts a specific mechanical rule (e.g. a fixed posting-time or per-day Reels cap) with no located official statement
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the folklore firewall: tag the claim ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN, exclude it from the standing playbook, and prefer the account's own Insights data once available

edge_cases.description: The account structure resolves to a two-account split before Collab-post cross-promotion between the two new accounts is set up.
edge_cases.trigger: ACCOUNT_STRUCTURE_DECISION resolves to split while both personas still share one flagship account's followers
edge_cases.mitigation: stand up Collab posts between the two new accounts at split time so neither loses the shared engagement pool

edge_cases.description: A photoreal persona post is scheduled without the AI self-label toggle applied.
edge_cases.trigger: the share screen's add-AI-label step is skipped during a rushed publish
edge_cases.mitigation: block publish at the workflow gate until the AI-label toggle is confirmed set, since this account's content is squarely in the mandatory-disclosure class

edge_cases.description: Fitness/swimwear content on either persona drifts toward a sexually-suggestive read and loses Explore/Reels recommendation eligibility.
edge_cases.trigger: the in-app account-status screen shows reduced recommendation eligibility after a run of physique-forward posts
edge_cases.mitigation: pull back toward the aspirational-fitness register the niche lock defines and watch the in-app recommendation-eligibility status, since the exact classifier threshold is unpublished

edge_cases.description: A visible third-party watermark survives into an exported Reel from the production pipeline.
edge_cases.trigger: an export path bypasses the clean-render requirement before posting
edge_cases.mitigation: add a pre-publish watermark check to the export gate so no Reel carrying a visible third-party mark reaches the recommendation surface

edge_cases.description: The bio/name-field keyword phrasing duplicates or contradicts the grid's visual-contract promise.
edge_cases.trigger: a bio rewrite ships independently of a grid/LUT change
edge_cases.mitigation: review bio and grid together at every identity-system revision, per the sequence tying bio and name-field authoring together

edge_cases.description: Google/Bing indexing of public captions surfaces a caption that reads fine in-app but poorly as a standalone search snippet.
edge_cases.trigger: a caption written purely as an in-persona voice line carries no searchable-sentence content at all
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the searchable-sentence-first-line convention even for in-voice captions so the indexed snippet still reads as a discoverable sentence

workflow.action: Lock the niche and name the cinematic-production-value differentiator
workflow.description: Fix the hybrid motivation+luxury(+fitness-accent) pillar, the classic-luxurious register and the differentiator against similar creator archetypes.
workflow.gate: the statement names the hybrid pillar and the differentiator, tagged ESTIMATE where it is a strategic judgment

workflow.action: Translate the owner's aspirational brief into a content-identity statement
workflow.description: Write the felt promise the bio, grid and highlights must each be checkable against.
workflow.gate: the statement is specific enough to rule some bio/grid choices out, not a generic aspiration

workflow.action: Decide one-account-vs-two for the two personas
workflow.description: Weigh shared momentum against persona-specific audience clarity and set the default plus split trigger.
workflow.gate: the decision states the one-account default and the explicit Insights-based trigger for a later split

workflow.action: Write the name-field keyword phrase and the 3-line bio skeleton together
workflow.description: Draft the name field and bio in one pass so they read as a single identity string naming both personas.
workflow.gate: line 1 states the category promise, line 2 names both personas, line 3 carries a CTA, and the name field carries a keyword phrase

workflow.action: Lock the grid's classic-luxe color-grade LUT family for the first 9-12 posts
workflow.description: Cross-check the proposed LUT family against the persona bible before committing.
workflow.gate: the LUT family is named and verified against the character-consistency specialist's locked grade, not set independently

workflow.action: Build the six-category highlight taxonomy including the BTS-AI transparency highlight
workflow.description: Name Him/Her/Places/Cars/Quotes/BTS-AI so each echoes the bio's vocabulary.
workflow.gate: all six categories are named and the BTS-AI highlight is present as a disclosure surface

workflow.action: Confirm the AI-info self-label step at the publish-checklist gate
workflow.description: Add a hard block on publish until the AI-label toggle is confirmed for every photoreal post.
workflow.gate: no post can publish without the add-AI-label toggle confirmed set

workflow.action: Assign Reels, carousels and Stories their discovery/depth/retention roles
workflow.description: Justify each format's role by the platform-stated signal it is judged on.
workflow.gate: each format cites the specific Mosseri signal (sends/reach, likes/reach, watch time, or closeness) it is judged against

workflow.action: Set the cold-start cadence baseline citing Mosseri's sustainability caveat
workflow.description: Fix the weeks 1-4 posting frequency at a level the operation can sustain past the starter window.
workflow.gate: the cadence does not exceed what the owner/operation can maintain past the 4-week window

workflow.action: Screen every proposed cadence/format rule through the folklore firewall before it enters the standing playbook
workflow.description: Tag each rule FACT/FACT-excerpt/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at the point of adoption.
workflow.gate: every rule entering the playbook carries its honesty tag and no unsourced creator-guru claim is encoded as a hard rule

dominance_rules.rule: When Mosseri's stated ranking signals conflict with a third-party benchmark's implied strategy, the platform-stated signal wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: third-party benchmarks are correlational cross-industry aggregates, not the actual ranking input Instagram uses
dominance_rules.trigger: a format-mix decision cites a benchmark that contradicts a named Mosseri signal
dominance_rules.action: discard or demote the benchmark-driven recommendation; keep the signal-driven one

dominance_rules.rule: When an aggregate best-time-to-post study conflicts with the account's own Insights 'most active times' data (once 2-4 weeks exist), own-account data wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: aggregate studies are cross-industry averages biased toward US/EU business audiences, low-medium confidence for this specific audience
dominance_rules.trigger: own Insights data exists and diverges from the aggregate window
dominance_rules.action: re-slot posting times to the account's own active-times window

dominance_rules.rule: When a creator-guru cadence/engagement claim has no located official Instagram statement, the folklore firewall wins over the claim.
dominance_rules.rationale: unsourced practitioner claims have produced no verifiable official source in this research pass
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim like a fixed engagement window or a per-day Reels posting cap surfaces
dominance_rules.action: tag it folklore/ESTIMATE-or-UNKNOWN and exclude it from the standing playbook

dominance_rules.rule: When the grid's visual-contract promise conflicts with the persona bible's locked wardrobe/hair/grade, the persona bible wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: the media manager consumes the persona bible and never improvises character identity independently
dominance_rules.trigger: a grid LUT or wardrobe choice diverges from the bible
dominance_rules.action: revise the grid plan to match the bible, not the reverse

dominance_rules.rule: When voluntary AI-transparency framing conflicts with a push for seamless cinematic illusion, mandatory disclosure wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: photorealistic AI video sits in Meta's mandatory-disclosure class; compliance outranks aesthetic seamlessness
dominance_rules.trigger: a creative pitch proposes hiding or downplaying the AI-generated nature of a photoreal post
dominance_rules.action: keep the self-label and the BTS-AI highlight regardless of the aesthetic argument

dominance_rules.rule: When cadence ambition conflicts with Mosseri's stated sustainability caveat, sustainability wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: Mosseri explicitly prefers twice-weekly-for-two-years over daily-for-two-months-then-quit
dominance_rules.trigger: a calendar draft exceeds what the operation can sustain past the 4-week starter window
dominance_rules.action: scale the cadence back to the sustainable baseline even if it forgoes short-term reach

dominance_rules.rule: When physique/fitness content's aspirational framing conflicts with a sexually-suggestive read that risks recommendation eligibility, the aspirational-fitness register wins.
dominance_rules.rationale: Instagram's Recommendation Guidelines exclude sexually suggestive content from Explore/Reels non-follower distribution even without a removal violation
dominance_rules.trigger: a physique-forward post is ambiguous between aspirational and sexually suggestive
dominance_rules.action: revise toward the aspirational-fitness/swimwear register and monitor the in-app recommendation-eligibility status

dominance_rules.rule: When the one-account default conflicts with an early anecdotal sense that personas should split, the one-flagship-account default wins until Insights show real divergence.
dominance_rules.rationale: splitting early doubles content burden and forfeits shared early momentum without evidence of divergence
dominance_rules.trigger: someone proposes splitting the account based on personal preference alone
dominance_rules.action: keep the one-account default; require a documented Insights-based split trigger before acting

dominance_rules.rule: When keyword-rich caption/name-field SEO phrasing conflicts with in-persona diegetic voice, write the SEO content inside the persona's voice rather than dropping the voice.
dominance_rules.rationale: captions are simultaneously a discovery surface and a brand-voice surface; sacrificing voice entirely undermines the identity system the whole KB is built on
dominance_rules.trigger: an SEO-optimized caption reads like a generic marketing sentence instead of the persona speaking
dominance_rules.action: rewrite the caption as a searchable sentence the persona would plausibly say

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock the niche and identity translation before drafting any bio or grid content.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rewriting bio/grid copy from scratch after realizing it does not match the actual niche/identity decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the account-structure decision (one vs two) before building persona-specific highlight taxonomies or handles.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building two separate highlight/handle sets that must be merged or discarded once the account-structure decision resolves to one account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cross-check every grid/LUT decision against the character-consistency specialist's persona bible before publishing the first 9-12 posts.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-grading or reshooting an already-published grid run because it drifted from the locked persona look

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the bio skeleton and the name-field keyword phrase in the same authoring pass.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a bio revision that contradicts or duplicates a name-field phrase drafted separately, forcing a second identity-system pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen every cadence/format claim through the folklore firewall before it enters the standing playbook, not after it has already shaped a published calendar.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: publishing weeks of calendar content on an unsourced folklore rule, then having to retract or re-explain the change to the owner

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the AI-info label toggle at the publish-checklist gate for every photoreal post, before the post goes live.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a retroactive edit/relabel of an already-published post once a compliance gap is noticed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat aggregate third-party timing/format benchmarks as a cold-start default only, and switch to the account's own Insights data as soon as 2-4 weeks of data exist.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: clinging to a stale aggregate-benchmark schedule long after the account's own data contradicts it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the Collab-post cross-promotion plan at the same time as the account-structure decision, not after a split has already happened.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a late scramble to rebuild the shared engagement pool after the two accounts have already diverged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve the watermark/clean-export check at the pipeline's export gate, not at the point of posting.
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a watermarked Reel only after it has already been posted and recommendation-penalized

iteration_protocol.trigger: the weekly analytics review shows a persona-attributed performance split
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the account-structure decision using the documented divergence threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: the account crosses the ~1,000-follower Trial Reels eligibility gate
iteration_protocol.action: fold Trial Reels experiments into the format division of labor as the new A/B mechanism for hook/persona/format testing

iteration_protocol.trigger: Instagram publishes a new or revised official ranking-explainer statement
iteration_protocol.action: re-fetch and re-verify the ranking model and Mosseri-signal nodes directly against the new official source before propagating changes

iteration_protocol.trigger: the persona bible is revised after the grid visual contract has already published posts under the old grade
iteration_protocol.action: frame the change as a deliberate 'new era' grid reset, not a silent retrofit, and update the grid-lock artifact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new creator-guru cadence/engagement claim surfaces from any source
iteration_protocol.action: run it through the folklore-firewall check and tag FACT/FACT-excerpt/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN before any playbook change

iteration_protocol.trigger: an in-app recommendation-eligibility warning appears on the account status screen
iteration_protocol.action: pull back the offending pillar toward the aspirational-fitness/niche register and log the incident for the weekly review

iteration_protocol.trigger: 2-4 weeks of the account's own Insights 'most active times' data accumulate
iteration_protocol.action: replace the aggregate cold-start posting-slot default with the account's own active-times window

iteration_protocol.trigger: Google/Bing indexing behavior or caption-search mechanics change
iteration_protocol.action: re-audit the caption-search-surface convention (searchable-sentence-first-line) against the new mechanics

priority_rationale: Foundational positioning decisions (niche lock, identity translation, two-persona architecture, account structure) and the ranking-model facts they depend on (no-single-algorithm, Mosseri's named signals) are locked first because every identity-system artifact and every format assignment is checked against them; compliance-critical nodes (AI-info labeling, impersonation boundary) carry the highest final_importance because their risk_if_wrong is highest and their failure is the least reversible.
